name: First-K Truncated IS
tagline: Per-token PPO clipped objective for the first K=64 response tokens; for later positions the importance ratio is detached so it carries no gradient.
pseudocode:
1. $\Delta = \mathrm{clip}(\log\pi_\theta - \log\pi_{\text{old}}, -20, 20)$, $r = e^{\Delta}$.
2. $m_t = \mathbb{1}[t < K]$ with $K=64$.
3. $r_{\text{eff}} = r\cdot m + r.\text{detach}()\cdot(1-m)$.
4. $\ell^{(1)} = -A\cdot r_{\text{eff}};\;\; \ell^{(2)} = -A\cdot \mathrm{clip}(r_{\text{eff}}, 1-\epsilon_l, 1+\epsilon_h)$.
5. $\ell = \max(\ell^{(1)}, \ell^{(2)})$ ; (optional rollout IS weights).
6. Aggregate via `agg_loss(loss_agg_mode="token-mean")`.

key_hyperparams.name: K
key_hyperparams.role: prefix length with live IS gradient

diff_from_baseline: Inspired by DAPO-style truncated/decoupled clipping (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14476). Late tokens drift the most in old-vs-new log-prob, so freezing their ratios kills the noisy IS gradient while keeping the per-token log_prob path intact for shorter responses.

name: Sequence-Level IS (GSPO)
tagline: One scalar importance ratio per response (masked mean of per-token log-prob differences) broadcast to every token, with PPO clipping and seq-mean-token-mean aggregation.
diff_from_baseline: GSPO (Zheng et al. 2025, arXiv:2507.18071). Replaces per-token importance weights with one ratio per sampled sequence, dramatically reducing variance and matching the clip behavior at the response level. Implemented via a straight-through estimator so per-token log-prob gradients still flow.

name: Token-Level PPO (GRPO default)
tagline: Standard per-token PPO clipped objective with dual clip (lower bound at -A*c) and token-mean aggregation, as in vanilla GRPO actor loss.
diff_from_baseline: Schulman et al., PPO (2017). The GRPO/verl default `compute_policy_loss_vanilla`: per-token importance ratio, per-token clip with optional asymmetric bounds, and dual-clip lower limit when advantages are negative. Reference comparator for ratio-design proposals.
